content: Have you ever wanted an electric bike that easily transitions from the drudgery of urban asphalt to adventures in gravel and dirt? That’s what a subclass of so-called “electric SUV” (eSUV) e-bikes claims to do, with their wide, all-terrain tires and front and rear suspension, plus practical accessories like fenders and racks. So, that’s what I set out to test on a new TL Carbon e-bike from Amflow, the DJI offshoot that upended the mountain bike industry a few years ago with its incredibly small and powerful Avinox motors. After a month of testing in the heart of Amsterdam — including a three day bikepacking trip along coastal bicycle superhighways and single-track forest routes — I can confirm what you might already expect: there are compromises. But for €3499 / $3,899 you do get a crossover e-bike that can help you fetch groceries during the week and conquer trails on the weekend. [Product: Amflow TL Carbon eSUV e-bike | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841] I rode my first crossover in 2024 when Cowboy launched its appropriately named Cross. That e-bike, like the vast majority of SUV automobiles, is more at home on pavement than dirt. But it looks burly, which attracts a certain kind of buyer hoping for transference. Today, these eSUVs are more popular than ever. Canyon, for example, makes one. Specialized, too. As does Riese & Müller and now Amflow. The Amflow TL Carbon is built upon the same Avinox drive system that threw the electric mountain bike (eMTB) industry into a tizzy two years ago. The TL Carbon is a bit less powerful, sporty, and springy than the impressive Amflow PX Carbon Pro I tested over the summer, but its eMTB roots are undeniable.  [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4661.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4733.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4754-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] I tested the TL Carbon on a bikepacking adventure from Amsterdam to the island of Texel at the tip top of the Netherlands. The 170km trip was about 70 percent asphalt, 20 percent gravel and dirt, and 10 percent rutted, hilly, single-track dedicated to mountain bikers. I was more than a little nervous riding the latter on a 19.2kg (42.3lbs) bike loaded down with an 87kg (190lbs) rider and about 20kg (44lbs) of gear. But Amflow’s compact mid-drive Avinox M2 motor, with its 125Nm of torque and 1100W of max output, flattened long, technical hills that other mountain bikers (not loaded down with gear) had to hike. As an eSUV, the TL Carbon has bonafide off-road credentials. I was also pleased by the range I extracted from the 800Wh battery, despite bikepacking on a very windy weekend. Amflow offers an optional battery extender that adds 480Wh to the total capacity, but I didn’t miss it. I rode in a mix of modes, spending the vast majority of the time in battery-sipping Eco mode, only switching into the adaptive Auto mode when facing a strong headwind, and Trail only when trying to dominate a highly technical or steep single-track. On my longest day, I arrived at my destination with 22 percent charge remaining after riding 82.3km (51.1 miles). That works out to an exceptional 7.58Wh per km (or 12.2Wh per mile) for a bike carrying so much gear. And because the TL Carbon’s battery is removable unlike Amflow’s premium eMTB, it can be easily charged behind a bar, at a cafe, or inside a home. I had no problem finding public chargers along the way, but I’m blessed to live in a country with excellent bicycle infrastructure. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4840.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4861.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_4853.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all] Still, as an eMTB, the Amflow TL Carbon makes plenty of compromises. The 27.5-inch front wheel is fine in town but it doesn’t roll over roots and rocks as well as 29-inch wheels found on modern mountain bikes (there’s clearance to swap a 29er in if you want). The geometry is also more upright than many would want on a trail, and the suspension travel at the front and rear is relatively short, tuned more for potholes than 1-meter drop-offs (yet it handled those fine). And the things you definitely want on a city bike — like the TL Carbon’s integrated lighting, kickstand, bell, mudguards, front rack, and rear rack — are not designed for quick removal and add considerable weight to the otherwise lightweight (just 2.9kg) carbon-fiber frame. Removing everything to go full eMTB could take 30 minutes or more, and then again to return to city mode. If the Amflow TL Carbon is your only bike then it certainly gets the job done in urban environments. But it’s a little like putting leather seats and a stereo inside a WWII-era jeep and calling it a city car.  In town, the Amflow TL Carbon looks out of place. For one thing, it screams I’m expensive, and the gas shock, Fox branding, and wide knobby tires make it stand out from basic city bikes — not something you want in places where bicycle theft is a problem. I wouldn’t feel comfortable parking it on the street overnight which is otherwise the common thing to do in compact, bicycle cities like Amsterdam. Amflow does equip it with Apple Find My if you need to track it down. chineseContent: 您是否曾经想要一辆电动自行车，可以轻松地从城市沥青的苦差事过渡到砾石和泥土中的冒险？这就是所谓的“电动 SUV”(eSUV) 电动自行车的一个子类声称要做的事情，其宽大的全地形轮胎、前后悬架，以及挡泥板和行李架等实用配件。因此，这就是我在 Amflow 推出的一款新型 TL Carbon 电动自行车上进行测试的内容，Amflow 是 DJI 的分支机构，几年前凭借其极其小巧而强大的 Avinox 电机颠覆了山地自行车行业。经过在阿姆斯特丹市中心一个月的测试——包括沿着沿海自行车高速公路和单轨森林路线进行为期三天的自行车旅行——我可以证实你可能已经预料到的事情：有妥协。但只需花费 3499 欧元/3,899 美元，您就可以获得一辆跨界电动自行车，它可以帮助您在一周内取货并在周末征服小径。 [产品：Amflow TL Carbon eSUV 电动自行车 | https://www.amflowbikes.com/product/amflow-tl-carbon-800wh?vid=242841] 我在 2024 年骑了我的第一次跨界车，当时 Cowboy 推出了其恰当命名的 Cross。与绝大多数 SUV 汽车一样，这款电动自行车更适合在人行道上行驶，而不是在泥土中行驶。但它看起来魁梧，这吸引了某些希望转让的买家。如今，这些 eSUV 比以往任何时候都更受欢迎。例如，Canyon 就生产了一款。也很专业。 Riese & Müller 和现在的 Amflow 也是如此。 Amflow TL Carbon 采用相同的 Avinox 驱动系统，两年前该系统使电动山地自行车 (eMTB) 行业陷入混乱。与我在夏天测试过的令人印象深刻的 Amflow PX Carbon Pro 相比，TL Carbon 的动力、运动感和弹性稍差，但其 eMTB 根源是不可否认的。  [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/IMG_466
